Code Search代码搜索

章首装饰插图（纯装饰，已省略）。

Written by Alexander Neubeck and Ben St. John

作者：Alexander Neubeck、Ben St. John

Edited by Lisa Carey

编辑：Lisa Carey

Code Search is a tool for browsing and searching code at Google that consists of a frontend UI and various backend elements. Like many of the development tools at Google, it arose directly out of a need to scale to the size of the codebase. Code Search began as a combination of a grep-type tool for internal code with the ranking and UI of external Code Search. Its place as a key tool for Google developers was cemented by the integration of Kythe/Grok, which added cross-references and the ability to jump to symbol definitions.

Code Search 是 Google 内部用于浏览和搜索代码的工具，由一个前端 UI 与各种后端组件构成。与 Google 的许多开发工具一样，它直接源于“扩展到代码库规模”的需求。Code Search 最初是一个内部代码 grep 类工具与外部 Code Search 的排名及 UI 的结合体。它之所以成为 Google 开发者的关键工具，是因为集成了 Kythe/Grok——后者增加了交叉引用和跳转到符号定义的能力。

That integration changed its focus from searching to browsing code, and later development of Code Search was partly guided by a principle of answering the next question about code in a single click. Now such questions as Where is this symbol defined?, Where is it used?, How do I include it?, When was it added to the codebase?, and even ones like Fleet-wide, how many CPU cycles does it consume? are all answerable with one or two clicks.

那次集成把它的重心从“搜索”转向了“浏览代码”，后来 Code Search 的开发部分遵循一条原则：“一次点击就能回答关于代码的下一个问题。”如今，诸如“这个符号在哪里定义？”“它在哪里被使用？”“我该如何包含它？”“它是什么时候加入代码库的？”，甚至像“在整个 fleet 中，它消耗多少 CPU 周期？”这类问题，都能通过一两次点击得到解答。

In contrast to integrated development environments (IDEs) or code editors, Code Search is optimized for the use case of reading, understanding, and exploring code at scale. To do so, it relies heavily on cloud-based backends for searching content and resolving cross-references.

与集成开发环境（IDE）或代码编辑器不同，Code Search 针对大规模阅读、理解和探索代码的用例做了优化。为此，它重度依赖基于云的后端来搜索内容、解析交叉引用。

原书第 379 页

In this chapter, we will look at Code Search in more detail, including how Googlers use it as part of their developer workflows, why we chose to develop a separate web tool for code searching, and examine how it addresses the challenges of searching and browsing code at Google repository scale.

本章中，我们将更详细地考察 Code Search，包括 Google 工程师如何把它作为开发工作流的一部分、我们为什么选择为代码搜索开发一个独立的 Web 工具，以及它如何应对在 Google 仓库规模下搜索与浏览代码的挑战。

The Code Search UI · Code Search 的 UI

The search box is a central element of the Code Search UI (see Figure 17-1), and like web search, it has suggestions that developers can use for quick navigation to files, symbols, or directories. For more complex use cases, a results page with code snippets is returned. The search itself can be thought of as an instant find in files (like the Unix grep command) with relevance ranking and some code-specific enhancements like proper syntax highlighting, scope awareness, and awareness of comments and string literals. Search is also available from the command line and can be incorporated into other tools via a Remote Procedure Call (RPC) API. This comes in handy when post-processing is required or if the result set is too large for manual inspection.

搜索框是 Code Search UI 的核心元素（见图 17-1），与 Web 搜索一样，它带有“建议”功能，开发者可借此快速导航到文件、符号或目录。对于更复杂的用例，则返回一个带代码片段的结果页。搜索本身可以被看作一个即时的“在文件中查找”（类似 Unix 的 grep 命令），并带有相关性排名以及一些代码专用的增强，如恰当的语法高亮、作用域感知，以及对注释和字符串字面量的感知。搜索也可从命令行使用，并能通过远程过程调用（RPC）API 集成到其他工具中。当需要后处理、或结果集太大而无法人工检查时，这很方便。

When viewing a single file, most tokens are clickable to let the user quickly navigate to related information. For example, a function call will link to its function definition, an imported filename to the actual source file, or a bug ID in a comment to the corresponding bug report. This is powered by compiler-based indexing tools like Kythe. Clicking the symbol name opens a panel with all the places the symbol is used. Simi

查看单个文件时，大多数记号都是可点击的，让用户快速导航到相关信息。例如，一次函数调用会链接到它的函数定义，一个被导入的文件名会链接到实际源文件，注释中的 bug ID 会链接到相应的 bug 报告。这由 Kythe 这类基于编译器的索引工具驱动。点击符号名会打开一个面板，列出该符号被使用的所有位置。类似地，

larly, hovering over local variables in a function will highlight all occurrences of that variable in the implementation.

把鼠标悬停在函数内的局部变量上，会高亮该变量在实现中的所有出现。

Code Search also shows the history of a file, via its integration with Piper (see Chapter 16). This means seeing older versions of the file, which changes have affected it, who wrote them, jumping to them in Critique (see Chapter 19), diffing versions of files, and the classic blame view if desired. Even deleted files can be seen from a directory view.

通过与 Piper 的集成（见第 16 章），Code Search 还能展示一个文件的历史。这意味着可以看到该文件的旧版本、哪些变更影响过它、是谁写的、在 Critique 中跳转到那些变更（见第 19 章）、对文件各版本做 diff，以及在需要时看到经典的“blame”视图。即便是已删除的文件，也能从目录视图中看到。

How Do Googlers Use Code Search? · Google 工程师如何使用 Code Search？

Although similar functionality is available in other tools, Googlers still make heavy use of the Code Search UI for searching and file viewing and ultimately for understanding code. The tasks engineers try to complete with Code Search can be thought of as answering questions about code, and recurring intents become visible.

尽管其他工具也提供类似功能，Google 工程师仍然大量使用 Code Search UI 进行搜索、文件查看，并最终用于理解代码。工程师试图用 Code Search 完成的任务，可以被看作“回答关于代码的问题”，反复出现的意图由此变得可见。

Where? · 在哪里？

About 16% of Code Searches try to answer the question of where a specific piece of information exists in the codebase; for example, a function definition or configuration, all usages of an API, or just where a specific file is in the repository. These questions are very targeted and can be very precisely answered with either search queries or by following semantic links, like jump to symbol definition. Such questions often arise during larger tasks like refactorings/cleanups or when collaborating with other engineers on a project. Therefore, it is essential that these small knowledge gaps are addressed efficiently.

约 16% 的 Code Search 试图回答“某条具体信息在代码库的哪里”；例如一个函数定义或配置、某个 API 的所有用法，或者某个具体文件在仓库中的位置。这些问题非常有针对性，可以通过搜索查询、或通过跟随语义链接（如“跳转到符号定义”）被非常精确地回答。这类问题常出现在重构/清理这类较大任务中，或在与其他工程师协作项目时。因此，高效地填补这些小的知识空白至关重要。

Code Search provides two ways of helping: ranking the results, and a rich query language. Ranking addresses the common cases, and searches can be made very specific (e.g., restricting code paths, excluding languages, only considering functions) to deal with rarer cases.

Code Search 提供两种帮助方式：对结果排名，以及一种丰富的查询语言。排名解决常见情形，而搜索可以被做得非常具体（例如限制代码路径、排除语言、只考虑函数），以处理较罕见的情形。

The UI makes it easy to share a Code Search result with colleagues. So, for code reviews, you can simply include the link—for example, Have you considered using this specialized hash map: cool_hash.h? This is also very useful for documentation, in bug reports, and in postmortems and is the canonical way of referring to code

该 UI 让与同事分享一个 Code Search 结果变得容易。因此，在代码评审中，你可以直接附上链接——例如：“你考虑过使用这个专门的哈希表 cool_hash.h 吗？”这在文档、bug 报告和事后复盘（postmortem）中也非常有用，是引用代码的标准方式

within Google. Even older versions of the code can be referenced, so links can stay valid as the codebase evolves.

（在 Google 内部）。甚至可以引用代码的旧版本，因此随着代码库演进，链接仍能保持有效。

What? · 是什么？

Roughly one quarter of Code Searches are classic file browsing, to answer the question of what a specific part of the codebase is doing. These kinds of tasks are usually more exploratory, rather than locating a specific result. This is using Code Search to read the source, to better understand code before making a change, or to be able to understand someone else's change.

大约四分之一的 Code Search 是经典的文件浏览，用以回答“代码库某个具体部分在做什么”。这类任务通常更偏探索，而非定位某个具体结果。这是在用 Code Search 阅读源码、在做改动前更好地理解代码，或能够理解别人的改动。

To ease these kinds of tasks, Code Search introduced browsing via call hierarchies and quick navigation between related files (e.g., between header, implementation, test, and build files). This is about understanding code by easily answering each of the many questions a developer has when looking at it.

为了简化这类任务，Code Search 引入了通过调用层次浏览、以及在相关文件之间快速导航（例如头文件、实现、测试和构建文件之间）。这是关于：通过轻松回答开发者查看代码时脑中的许多问题中的每一个，来理解代码。

How? · 怎么做？

The most frequent use case—about one third of Code Searches—are about seeing examples of how others have done something. Typically, a developer has already found a specific API (e.g., how to read a file from remote storage) and wants to see how the API should be applied to a particular problem (e.g., how to set up the remote connection robustly and handle certain types of errors). Code Search is also used to find the proper library for specific problems in the first place (e.g., how to compute a fingerprint for integer values efficiently) and then pick the most appropriate implementation. For these kinds of tasks, a combination of searches and cross-reference browsing are typical.

最频繁的用例——约占 Code Search 的三分之一——是查看别人是如何做某件事的示例。典型情形是：开发者已经找到了一个具体 API（例如如何从远程存储读取文件），想看看该 API 应如何应用于某个具体问题（例如如何稳健地建立远程连接并处理某些类型的错误）。Code Search 也被用来首先为具体问题找到合适的库（例如如何高效计算整数值的指纹），然后挑选最合适的实现。对这类任务，搜索与交叉引用浏览的组合是典型做法。

Why? · 为什么？

Related to what code is doing, there are more targeted queries around why code is behaving differently than expected. About 16% of Code Searches try to answer the question of why a certain piece of code was added, or why it behaves in a certain way. Such questions often arise during debugging; for example, why does an error occur under these particular circumstances?

与“代码在做什么”相关，还有更有针对性的查询，围绕“代码为什么表现得与预期不同”。约 16% 的 Code Search 试图回答“为什么加入了某段代码”或“它为什么以某种方式表现”。这类问题常出现在调试中；例如，为什么在这些特定情况下会发生错误？

An important capability here is being able to search and explore the exact state of the codebase at a particular point in time. When debugging a production issue, this can mean working with a state of the codebase that is weeks or months old, while debugging test failures for new code usually means working with changes that are only minutes old. Both are possible with Code Search.

这里一项重要能力，是能够搜索并探索代码库在某个特定时间点的确切状态。调试生产问题时，这可能意味着要使用几周或几个月前的代码库状态；而为新代码调试测试失败时，通常意味着要使用只有几分钟历史的变更。这两种情形在 Code Search 中都可以实现。

原书第 382 页

Who and When? · 是谁、何时？

About 8% of Code Searches try to answer questions around who or when someone introduced a certain piece of code, interacting with the version control system. For example, it is possible to see when a particular line was introduced (like Git's blame) and jump to the relevant code review. This history panel can also be very useful in finding the best person to ask about the code, or to review a change to it.

约 8% 的 Code Search 试图回答关于“是谁、在何时引入了某段代码”的问题，这与版本控制系统交互。例如，可以看到某一行是何时被引入的（类似 Git 的 blame），并跳转到相关的代码评审。这个历史面板在找到“最适合问这段代码的人”或“评审对它的改动的人”时也非常有用。

Why a Separate Web Tool? · 为什么要做一个独立的 Web 工具？

Outside Google, most of the aforementioned investigations are done within a local IDE. So, why yet another tool?

在 Google 之外，上述大多数调查都是在本地 IDE 中完成的。那么，为什么还要再做一个工具？

Scale · 规模

The first answer is that the Google codebase is so large that a local copy of the full codebase—a prerequisite for most IDEs—simply does not fit on a single machine. Even before this fundamental barrier is hit, there is a cost to building local search and cross-reference indices for each developer, a cost often paid at IDE startup, slowing developer velocity. Or, without an index, one-off searches (e.g., with grep) can become painfully slow. A centralized search index means doing this work once, upfront, and means investments in the process benefit everyone. For example, the Code Search index is incrementally updated with every submitted change, enabling index construction with linear cost.

第一个答案是：Google 的代码库如此之大，以至于“完整代码库的本地副本”——这是大多数 IDE 的前提——根本装不进单机。即便还没碰到这道根本障碍，为每位开发者构建本地搜索与交叉引用索引也有成本，这个成本往往在 IDE 启动时支付，拖慢开发者速度。或者，没有索引时，一次性搜索（例如用 grep）会慢得难受。一个集中式搜索索引意味着一次性、 upfront 地做这项工作，意味着对该流程的投资让所有人受益。例如，Code Search 索引随着每次提交的变更被增量更新，从而以线性成本实现索引构建。

In normal web search, fast-changing current events are mixed with more slowly changing items, such as stable Wikipedia pages. The same technique can be extended to searching code, making indexing incremental, which reduces its cost and allows changes to the codebase to be visible to everyone instantly. When a code change is submitted, only the actual files touched need to be reindexed, which allows parallel and independent updates to the global index.

在普通 Web 搜索中，快速变化的时事与变化较慢的条目（如稳定的维基百科页面）混在一起。同样的技术可被扩展到搜索代码，使索引增量式进行，从而降低成本，并让代码库的变更对所有人即时可见。当一次代码变更被提交时，只有实际被改动的文件需要被重新索引，这允许对全局索引进行并行、独立的更新。

Unfortunately, the cross-reference index cannot be instantly updated in the same way. Incrementality is not possible for it, as any code change can potentially influence the entire codebase, and in practice often does affect thousands of files. Many (nearly all

遗憾的是，交叉引用索引无法以同样的方式即时更新。对它而言增量式是不可能的，因为任何代码变更都可能影响整个代码库，实践中常常确实影响数千个文件。许多（几乎所有

of Google's) full binaries need to be built (or at least analyzed) to determine the full semantic structure. It uses a ton of compute resources to produce the index daily (the current frequency). The discrepancy between the instant search index and the daily cross-reference index is a source of rare but recurring issues for users.

Google 的）完整二进制都需要被构建（或至少分析），才能确定完整的语义结构。它每天（当前频率）产出索引要耗费巨量计算资源。即时搜索索引与每日交叉引用索引之间的不一致，是用户遇到一些罕见但反复出现的问题的根源。

Zero Setup Global Code View · 零配置的全局代码视图

Being able to instantly and effectively browse the entire codebase means that it's very easy to find relevant libraries to reuse and good examples to copy. For IDEs that construct indices at startup, there is a pressure to have a small project or visible scope to reduce this time and avoid flooding tools like autocomplete with noise. With the Code Search web UI, there is no setup required (e.g., project descriptions, build environment), so it's also very easy and fast to learn about code, wherever it occurs, which improves developer efficiency. There's also no danger of missing code dependencies; for example, when updating an API, reducing merge and library versioning issues.

能够即时、高效地浏览整个代码库，意味着很容易找到可复用的相关库和可拷贝的好示例。对于在启动时构建索引的 IDE，存在一种压力：要让项目小一点、或可见范围小一点，以减少这一时间，并避免用噪声淹没自动补全之类的工具。用 Code Search 的 Web UI，无需任何配置（例如项目描述、构建环境），因此无论代码出现在哪里，了解它都非常容易、快速，从而提升开发者效率。也不存在遗漏代码依赖的危险；例如在更新 API 时，能减少合并与库版本问题。

Specialization · 专门化

Perhaps surprisingly, one advantage of Code Search is that it is not an IDE. This means that the user experience (UX) can be optimized for browsing and understanding code, rather than editing it, which is usually the bulk of an IDE (e.g., keyboard shortcuts, menus, mouse clicks, and even screen space). For example, because there isn't an editor's text cursor, every mouse click on a symbol can be made meaningful (e.g., show all usages or jump to definition), rather than as a way to move the cursor. This advantage is so large that it's extremely common for developers to have multiple Code Search tabs open at the same time as their editor.

或许令人意外，Code Search 的一个优势在于它不是 IDE。这意味着用户体验（UX）可以针对“浏览和理解代码”而非“编辑代码”来优化——后者通常占了 IDE 的大头（例如键盘快捷键、菜单、鼠标点击，乃至屏幕空间）。例如，因为没有编辑器的文本光标，每次在符号上的鼠标点击都可以被赋予意义（例如显示所有用法或跳转到定义），而不是用来移动光标。这个优势如此之大，以至于开发者在编辑器旁边同时打开多个 Code Search 标签页是极其常见的事。

Integration with Other Developer Tools · 与其他开发者工具的集成

Because it is the primary way to view source code, Code Search is the logical platform for exposing information about source code. It frees up tool creators from needing to create a UI for their results and ensures the entire developer audience will know of their work without needing to advertise it. Many analyses run regularly over the entire Google codebase, and their results are usually surfaced in Code Search. For

由于它是查看源代码的主要方式，Code Search 是展示源代码相关信息的合乎逻辑的平台。它把工具创建者从“需要为结果创建 UI”中解放出来，并确保全体开发者受众都会知道他们的工作，而无需为此做广告。许多分析会定期在整个 Google 代码库上运行，其结果通常呈现在 Code Search 中。例如，

原书第 384 页

example, for many languages, we can detect dead (uncalled) code and mark it as such when the file is browsed.

对许多语言，我们可以检测出“死的”（未被调用的）代码，并在浏览该文件时把它标记出来。

In the other direction, the Code Search link to a source file is considered its canonical location. This is useful for many developer tools (see Figure 17-2). For example, log file lines typically contain the filename and line number of the logging statement. The production log viewer uses a Code Search link to connect the log statement back to the producing code. Depending on the available information, this can be a direct link to a file at a specific revision, or a basic filename search with the corresponding line number. If there is only one matching file, it is opened at the corresponding line number. Otherwise, snippets of the desired line in each of the matching files are rendered.

在另一个方向上，指向一个源文件的 Code Search 链接被认为是它的规范“位置”。这对许多开发者工具都很有用（见图 17-2）。例如，日志文件行通常包含日志语句所在的文件名和行号。生产日志查看器使用一个 Code Search 链接，把日志语句连回产生它的代码。根据可用信息的不同，这可以是指向某个特定修订版本文件的直接链接，也可以是一个带相应行号的基本文件名搜索。如果只有一个匹配文件，它会在相应行号处被打开；否则，会渲染每个匹配文件中目标行的片段。

Similarly, stack frames are linked back to source code whether they are shown within a crash reporting tool or in log output, as shown in Figure 17-3. Depending on the programming language, the link will utilize a filename or symbol search. Because the snapshot of the repository at which the crashing binary was built is known, the search can actually be restricted to exactly this version. That way, links remain valid for a long time period, even if the corresponding code is later refactored or deleted.

类似地，无论栈帧显示在崩溃报告工具中还是在日志输出中，都会被链接回源代码，如图 17-3 所示。根据编程语言的不同，该链接会使用文件名或符号搜索。由于崩溃二进制构建时的仓库快照是已知的，搜索实际上可以被严格限制在这个版本。这样，即使相应代码后来被重构或删除，链接也能在很长时间内保持有效。

原书第 385 页

Compilation errors and tests also typically refer back to a code location (e.g., test X in file at line). These can be linkified even for unsubmitted code given that most development happens in specific cloud-visible workspaces that are accessible and searchable by Code Search.

编译错误和测试通常也会指回某个代码位置（例如文件中第 X 行的测试）。即便对未提交的代码，这些也可以被加上链接——因为大多数开发发生在特定的、对云可见的工作区中，而这些工作区可被 Code Search 访问和搜索。

Finally, codelabs and other documentation refer to APIs, examples, and implementations. Such links can be search queries referencing a specific class or function, which remain valid when the file structure changes. For code snippets, the most recent implementation at head can easily be embedded into a documentation page, as demonstrated in Figure 17-4, without the need to pollute the source file with additional documentation markers.

最后，codelab 和其他文档会引用 API、示例和实现。这样的链接可以是引用某个具体类或函数的搜索查询，当文件结构变化时仍然有效。对于代码片段，head 处的最新实现可以很容易地嵌入文档页面，如图 17-4 所示，而无需用额外的文档标记污染源文件。

原书第 386 页

API Exposure · API 暴露

Code Search exposes its search, cross-reference, and syntax highlighting APIs to tools, so tool developers can bring those capabilities into their tools without needing to reimplement them. Further, plug-ins have been written to provide search and cross-references to editors and IDEs such as vim, emacs, and IntelliJ. These plug-ins restore some of the power lost due to being unable to locally index the codebase, and give back some developer productivity.

Code Search 向工具暴露它的搜索、交叉引用和语法高亮 API，因此工具开发者可以把这些能力带入自己的工具，而无需重新实现。此外，还编写了一些插件，为 vim、emacs、IntelliJ 等编辑器和 IDE 提供搜索与交叉引用。这些插件恢复了一部分因无法在本地索引代码库而损失的能力，还回一部分开发者生产力。

Impact of Scale on Design · 规模对设计的影响

In the previous section, we looked at various aspects of the Code Search UI and why it's worthwhile having a separate tool for browsing code. In the following sections, we look a bit behind the scenes of the implementation. We first discuss the primary challenge—scaling—and then some of the ways the large scale complicates making a good product for searching and browsing code. After that, we detail how we addressed some of those challenges, and what trade-offs were made when building Code Search.

上一节中，我们考察了 Code Search UI 的各个方面、以及为什么值得为浏览代码做一个独立工具。在接下来的几节，我们稍微看看实现背后的情况。我们先讨论首要挑战——规模化——然后看看大规模在哪些方面让“打造一个好的代码搜索与浏览产品”变得复杂。之后，我们详述我们是如何应对其中一些挑战的，以及在构建 Code Search 时做了哪些权衡。

The biggest scaling challenge for searching code is the corpus size. For a small repository of a couple megabytes, a brute-force search with grep search will do. When hundreds of megabytes need to be searched, a simple local index can speed up search by an order of magnitude or more. When gigabytes or terabytes of source code need to be searched, a cloud-hosted solution with multiple machines can keep search times reasonable. The utility of a central solution increases with the number of developers using it and the size of the code space.

搜索代码最大的规模化挑战是语料库大小。对于几 MB 的小仓库，用 grep 暴力搜索就够了。当需要搜索数百 MB 时，一个简单的本地索引可以把搜索加速一个数量级或更多。当需要搜索 GB 乃至 TB 级源代码时，一个由多台机构成的云端托管方案才能把搜索时间保持在合理范围。集中式方案的效用，随使用它的开发者数量和代码空间大小而增长。

Search Query Latency · 搜索查询延迟

Although we take as a given that a fast and responsive UI is better for the user, low latency doesn't come for free. To justify the effort, one can weigh it against the saved engineering time across all users. Within Google, we process much more than one million search queries from developers within Code Search per day. For one million queries, an increase of just one second per search request corresponds to about 35 idle full-time engineers every day. In contrast, the search backend can be built and maintained with roughly a tenth of these engineers. This means that with about 100,000 queries per day (corresponding to less than 5,000 developers), just the one-second latency argument is something of a break-even point.

尽管我们把“快速、响应灵敏的 UI 对用户更好”视为理所当然，但低延迟不是免费来的。为了证明这些努力值得，可以把它与在所有用户身上节省的工程时间相权衡。在 Google，我们每天在 Code Search 中处理来自开发者的查询远超过一百万次。对一百万次查询而言，每次搜索请求仅增加 1 秒，就相当于每天约 35 名闲置的全职工程师。相比之下，构建和维护搜索后端大约只需这些工程师的十分之一。这意味着：每天约 10 万次查询（对应不到 5000 名开发者）时，单是那“1 秒延迟”的论点就大致是一个盈亏平衡点。

In reality, the productivity loss doesn't simply increase linearly with latency. A UI is considered responsive if latencies are below 200 ms. But after just one second, the developer's attention often begins to drift. If another 10 seconds pass, the developer is

现实中，生产力损失并不随延迟简单线性增长。如果延迟低于 200 ms，UI 就被认为是响应灵敏的。但只要过了 1 秒，开发者的注意力常常就开始涣散。如果再过 10 秒，开发者就

原书第 387 页

likely to switch context completely, which is generally recognized to have high productivity costs. The best way to keep a developer in the productive flow state is by targeting sub–200 ms end-to-end latency for all frequent operations and investing in the corresponding backends.

很可能完全切换上下文，而这被公认为有很高的生产力代价。让开发者保持在高效“心流”状态的最佳方式，是让所有频繁操作的端到端延迟都瞄准 200 ms 以下，并在相应后端上投资。

A large number of Code Search queries are performed in order to navigate the codebase. Ideally, the next file is only a click away (e.g., for included files, or symbol definitions), but for general navigation, instead of using the classical file tree, it can be much faster to simply search for the desired file or symbol, ideally without needing to fully specify it, and suggestions are provided for partial text. This becomes increasingly true as the codebase (and file tree) grows.

大量 Code Search 查询是为了在代码库中导航。理想情况下，“下一个”文件只需一次点击（例如对被包含文件或符号定义）；但对于一般导航，与其使用经典文件树，不如直接搜索想要的文件或符号——理想情况下无需完整指定它，对部分文本还会提供建议——要快得多。随着代码库（和文件树）增长，这一点愈发成立。

Normal navigation to a specific file in another folder or project requires several user interactions. With search, just a couple of keystrokes can be sufficient to get to the relevant file. To make search this effective, additional information about the search context (e.g., the currently viewed file) can be provided to the search backend. The context can restrict the search to files of a specific project, or influence ranking by preferring files that are in proximity to other files or directories. In the Code Search UI, the user can predefine multiple contexts and quickly switch between them as needed. In editors, the open or edited files are implicitly used as context to prioritize search results in their proximity.

普通导航到另一个文件夹或项目中的某个具体文件，需要若干次用户交互。用搜索，只需几次击键就可能到达相关文件。为了让搜索如此有效，可以把关于搜索上下文的附加信息（例如当前查看的文件）提供给搜索后端。该上下文可以把搜索限制在某个具体项目的文件内，或通过偏爱与其他文件、目录邻近的文件来影响排名。在 Code Search UI 中，用户可以预定义多个上下文，并在需要时快速切换。在编辑器中，打开或正在编辑的文件被隐式用作上下文，以优先考虑附近的搜索结果。

One could consider the power of the search query language (e.g., specifying files, using regular expressions) as another criteria; we discuss this in the trade-offs section a little later in the chapter.

人们可以把搜索查询语言的能力（例如指定文件、使用正则表达式）视为另一个评判标准；我们在本章稍后的权衡一节中讨论它。

Index Latency · 索引延迟

Most of the time, developers won't notice when indices are out of date. They only care about a small subset of code, and even for that they generally won't know whether there is more recent code. However, for the cases in which they wrote or reviewed the corresponding change, being out of sync can cause a lot of confusion. It tends not to matter whether the change was a small fix, a refactoring, or a completely new piece of code—developers simply expect a consistent view, such as they experience in their IDE for a small project.

大多数时候，开发者不会注意到索引已过时。他们只关心代码的一小部分，即便对那部分，他们通常也不知道是否有更新的代码。然而，对于那些他们自己写过或评审过相应变更的情形，不同步会造成很大困惑。无论那变更是个小修复、一次重构，还是一整段全新代码，往往都不重要——开发者就是期望一个一致的视图，就像他们在 IDE 里面对一个小项目时所体验的那样。

When writing code, instant indexing of modified code is expected. When new files, functions, or classes are added, not being able to find them is frustrating and breaks the normal workflow for developers used to perfect cross-referencing. Another example are search-and-replace–based refactorings. It is not only more convenient when the removed code immediately disappears from the search results, but it is also essential that subsequent refactorings take the new state into account. When working with

写代码时，被修改的代码被即时索引是预期之内的。当新增文件、函数或类时，找不到它们会令人沮丧，并打断习惯了完美交叉引用的开发者的正常工作流。另一个例子是基于搜索—替换的重构。当被删除的代码立即从搜索结果中消失时，不仅更方便，而且后续重构必须考虑新状态，这一点至关重要。在使用

原书第 388 页

a centralized VCS, a developer might need instant indexing for submitted code if the previous change is no longer part of the locally modified file set.

集中式 VCS 时，如果上一次变更已不再属于本地被修改的文件集合，开发者可能需要对已提交代码的即时索引。

Conversely, sometimes it's useful to be able to go back in time to a previous snapshot of the code; in other words, a release. During an incident, a discrepancy between the index and the running code can be especially problematic because it can hide real causes or introduce irrelevant distractions. This is a problem for cross-references because the current technology for building an index at Google's scale simply takes hours, and the complexity means that only one version of the index is kept. Although some patching can be done to align new code with an old index, this is still an issue to be solved.

反过来，有时能够回到代码的先前快照是有用的；换言之，回到一次发布。在事故期间，索引与运行代码之间的不一致可能尤其成问题，因为它可能掩盖真正的原因、或引入无关的干扰。这对交叉引用是个问题，因为在 Google 规模下构建索引的当前技术要花数小时，而其复杂性意味着只保留一个版本的索引。虽然可以做一些补丁来让新代码与旧索引对齐，但这仍是一个待解决的问题。

Google's Implementation · Google 的实现

Google's particular implementation of Code Search is tailored to the unique characteristics of its codebase, and the previous section outlined our design constraints for creating a robust and responsive index. The following section outlines how the Code Search team implemented and released its tool to Google developers.

Google 对 Code Search 的特定实现是为其代码库的独特特征量身定制的，上一节概述了我们创建一个健壮、响应灵敏的索引时所面临的设计约束。下一节概述 Code Search 团队是如何实现并向 Google 开发者发布其工具的。

Search Index · 搜索索引

Google's codebase is a special challenge for Code Search due to its sheer size. In the early days, a trigram-based approach was taken. Russ Cox subsequently open sourced a simplified version. Currently, Code Search indexes about 1.5 TB of content and processes about 200 queries per second with a median server-side search latency of less than 50 ms and a median indexing latency (time between code commit and visibility in the index) of less than 10 seconds.

由于体量庞大，Google 的代码库对 Code Search 是一项特殊挑战。早期采用了基于三元组（trigram）的方法，Russ Cox 随后开源了一个简化版本。目前，Code Search 索引约 1.5 TB 的内容，每秒处理约 200 次查询，服务器端搜索延迟中位数低于 50 ms，索引延迟（从代码提交到在索引中可见的时间）中位数低于 10 秒。

Let's roughly estimate the resource requirements to achieve this performance with a grep-based brute-force solution. The RE2 library we use for regular expression matching processes about 100 MB/sec for data in RAM. Given a time window of 50 ms, 300,000 cores would be needed to crunch through the 1.5 TB of data. Because in most cases simple substring searches are sufficient, one could replace the regular expression matching with a special substring search that can process about 1 GB/sec under certain conditions, reducing the number of cores by 10 times. So far, we have looked at just the resource requirements for processing a single query within 50 ms. If we're getting 200 requests per second, 10 of those will be simultaneously active in that 50 ms window, bringing us back to 300,000 cores just for substring search.

让我们粗略估计一下：用基于 grep 的暴力方案来达到这种性能，需要多少资源。我们用于正则匹配的 RE2 库对 RAM 中数据的处理速度约为 100 MB/秒。给定 50 ms 的时间窗口，要处理完 1.5 TB 数据，需要 30 万个核。由于大多数情况下简单子串搜索就够了，可以用一种特殊子串搜索替换正则匹配，它在某些条件下能处理约 1 GB/秒，把核数减少 10 倍。到目前为止，我们只考虑了在 50 ms 内处理单个查询的资源需求。如果我们每秒收到 200 个请求，那么在那个 50 ms 窗口内会有 10 个同时活跃，又把我们拉回到仅子串搜索就需要 30 万核。

原书第 389 页

Although this estimate ignores that the search can stop once a certain number of results are found or that file restrictions can be evaluated much more effectively than content searches, it doesn't take communication overhead, ranking, or the fan out to tens of thousands of machines into account either. But it shows quite well the scale involved and why Google's Code Search team continuously invests into improving indexing. Over the years, our index changed from the original trigram-based solution, through a custom suffix array–based solution, to the current sparse n-gram solution. This latest solution is more than 500 times more efficient than the brute-force solution while being capable of also answering regular expression searches at blazing speed.

尽管这个估计忽略了“一旦找到一定数量结果搜索就可停止”或“文件限制比内容搜索评估起来高效得多”，它也没有把通信开销、排名、或向数万台机器的扇出算进去。但它很好地说明了所涉及的规模，以及为什么 Google 的 Code Search 团队持续投资改进索引。多年来，我们的索引从最初基于三元组的方案，经过自定义的基于后缀数组的方案，演变到当前的稀疏 n-gram 方案。最新这个方案比暴力方案高效 500 倍以上，同时还能以极快速度回答正则表达式搜索。

One reason we moved from a suffix array–based solution to a token-based n-gram solution was to take advantage of Google's primary indexing and search stack. With a suffix array–based solution, building and distributing the custom indices becomes a challenge in and of itself. By utilizing standard technology, we benefit from all the advances in reverse index construction, encoding, and serving made by the core search team. Instant indexing is another feature that exists in standard search stacks, and by itself is a big challenge when solving it at scale.

我们从基于后缀数组的方案转向基于记号（token）的 n-gram 方案，原因之一是为了利用 Google 主流的索引与搜索栈。用基于后缀数组的方案，构建和分发自定义索引本身就成了一项挑战。通过利用“标准”技术，我们受益于核心搜索团队在倒排索引构建、编码和服务上的所有进展。即时索引是标准搜索栈中已有的另一项特性，而在规模化下解决它本身就是一大挑战。

Relying on standard technology is a trade-off between implementation simplicity and performance. Even though Google's Code Search implementation is based on standard reverse indices, the actual retrieval, matching, and scoring are highly customized and optimized. Some of the more advanced Code Search features wouldn't be possible otherwise. To index the history of file revisions, we came up with a custom compression scheme in which indexing the full history increased the resource consumption by a factor of just 2.5.

依赖标准技术是在实现简洁性与性能之间的权衡。尽管 Google 的 Code Search 实现基于标准倒排索引，但实际的检索、匹配和打分都是高度定制和优化的。否则，Code Search 一些较高级的特性将无法实现。为了索引文件修订的历史，我们想出了一种自定义压缩方案，在该方案中，索引完整历史仅使资源消耗增加 2.5 倍。

In the early days, Code Search served all data from memory. With the growing index size, we moved the inverted index to flash. Although flash storage is at least an order of magnitude cheaper than memory, its access latency is at least two orders of magnitude higher. So, indices that work well in memory might not be suitable when served from flash. For instance, the original trigram index requires fetching not only a large number of reverse indices from flash, but also quite large ones. With n-gram schemes, both the number of inverse indices and their size can be reduced at the expense of a larger index.

早期，Code Search 从内存提供所有数据。随着索引增大，我们把倒排索引移到了闪存。尽管闪存至少比内存便宜一个数量级，但它的访问延迟至少高两个数量级。因此，在内存中运转良好的索引，在闪存上服务时可能并不合适。例如，最初的三元组索引不仅需要从闪存拉取大量倒排索引，而且这些索引还相当大。用 n-gram 方案，可以以更大的索引为代价，减少倒排索引的数量及其大小。

To support local workspaces (which have a small delta from the global repository), we have multiple machines doing simple brute-force searches. The workspace data is loaded on the first request and then kept in sync by listening for file changes. When we run out of memory, we remove the least recent workspace from the machines. The unchanged documents are searched with our history index. Therefore, the search is implicitly restricted to the repository state to which the workspace is synced.

为了支持本地工作区（它们与全局仓库只有很小的差异），我们有多台机器在做简单的暴力搜索。工作区数据在第一次请求时被加载，然后通过监听文件变化保持同步。当内存用尽时，我们把最久未用的工作区从机器上移除。未变更的文档用我们的历史索引搜索。因此，搜索被隐式限制在该工作区所同步到的仓库状态。

原书第 390 页

Ranking · 排名

For a very small codebase, ranking doesn't provide much benefit, because there aren't many results anyway. But the larger the codebase becomes, the more results will be found and the more important ranking becomes. In Google's codebase, any short substring will occur thousands, if not millions, of times. Without ranking, the user either must check all of those results in order to find the correct one, or must refine the query further until the result set is reduced to just a handful of files. Both options waste the developer's time.

对于非常小的代码库，排名带来的收益不大，因为结果本来就不多。但代码库越大，找到的结果越多，排名就越重要。在 Google 的代码库中，任何短子串都会出现数千次乃至数百万次。没有排名，用户要么必须检查所有那些结果才能找到正确的那个，要么必须进一步精化查询，直到结果集缩小到只有寥寥几个文件。两种选择都浪费开发者的时间。

Ranking typically starts with a scoring function, which maps a set of features of each file (signals) to some number: the higher the score, the better the result. The goal of the search is then to find the top N results as efficiently as possible. Typically, one distinguishes between two types of signals: those that depend only on the document (query independent) and those that depend on the search query and how it matches the document (query dependent). The filename length or the programming language of a file would be examples of query independent signals, whereas whether a match is a function definition or a string literal is a query dependent signal.

排名通常从一个打分函数开始，该函数把每个文件的一组特征（信号）映射到某个数值：分数越高，结果越好。搜索的目标就是尽可能高效地找到前 N 个结果。通常区分两类信号：只依赖于文档的（与查询无关），以及依赖于搜索查询及其与文档匹配方式的（与查询相关）。文件名长度、文件所用的编程语言，是与查询无关信号的例子；而一次匹配是函数定义还是字符串字面量，则是与查询相关的信号。

Query independent signals · 与查询无关的信号

Some of the most important query independent signals are the number of file views and the amount of references to a file. File views are important because they indicate which files developers consider important and are therefore more likely to want to find. For instance, utility functions in base libraries have a high view count. It doesn't matter whether the library is already stable and isn't changed anymore or whether the library is being actively developed. The biggest downside of this signal is the feedback loop it creates. By scoring frequently viewed documents higher, the chance increases that developers will look at them and decreases the chance of other documents to make it into the top N. This problem is known as exploitation versus exploration, for which various solutions exist (e.g., advanced A/B search experiments or curation of training data). In practice, it doesn't seem harmful to somewhat over-show high-scoring items: they are simply ignored when irrelevant and taken if a generic example is needed. However, it is a problem for new files, which don't yet have enough information for a good signal.

一些最重要的与查询无关信号，是文件被查看的次数以及对一个文件的引用数量。文件查看次数之所以重要，是因为它表明哪些文件被开发者认为重要、因而更可能想被找到。例如，基础库中的工具函数查看数很高。无论该库已经稳定、不再变化，还是正在被积极开发，都没关系。这个信号最大的弊端是它造成的反馈回路。通过给频繁被查看的文档更高分数，开发者查看它们的机会增加，而其他文档进入前 N 名的机会减少。这个问题被称为“利用与探索”（exploitation versus exploration），对此有各种解决方案（例如高级 A/B 搜索实验或训练数据的甄选）。实践中，稍微过度展示高分项目似乎并无害处：无关时它们直接被忽略，需要通用示例时又会被采用。然而，这对新文件是个问题，它们还没有足够信息形成好的信号。

We also use the number of references to a file, which parallels the original page rank algorithm, by replacing web links as references with the various kinds of include/import statements present in most languages. We can extend the concept up to build

我们还使用对一个文件的引用数量，这与最初的 page rank 算法平行——把 Web 链接作为引用，替换为大多数语言中出现的各种 include/import 语句。我们可以把这个概念向上扩展到构建

原书第 391 页

dependencies (library/module level references) and down to functions and classes. This global relevance is often referred to as the document's priority.

依赖（库/模块级引用），向下扩展到函数和类。这种全局相关性常被称为文档的“优先级”。

When using references for ranking, one must be aware of two challenges. First, you must be able to extract reference information reliably. In the early days, Google's Code Search extracted include/import statements with simple regular expressions and then applied heuristics to convert them into full file paths. With the growing complexity of a codebase, such heuristics became error prone and challenging to maintain. Internally, we replaced this part with correct information from the Kythe graph.

使用引用做排名时，必须注意两个挑战。第一，你必须能够可靠地提取引用信息。早期，Google 的 Code Search 用简单正则表达式提取 include/import 语句，然后应用启发式把它们转换为完整文件路径。随着代码库日益复杂，这类启发式变得容易出错、难以维护。在内部，我们用来自 Kythe 图的正确信息替换了这部分。

Large-scale refactorings, such as open sourcing core libraries, present a second challenge. Such changes don't happen atomically in a single code update; rather, they need to be rolled out in multiple stages. Typically, indirections are introduced, hiding, for example, the move of files from usages. These kinds of indirections reduce the page rank of moved files and make it more difficult for developers to discover the new location. Additionally, file views usually become lost when files are moved, making the situation even worse. Because such global restructurings of the codebase are comparatively rare (most interfaces move rarely), the simplest solution is to manually boost files during such transition periods. (Or wait until the migration completes and for the natural processes to up-rank the file in its new location.)

大规模重构（例如把核心库开源）带来第二个挑战。这类变更不会在一次代码更新中原子发生；相反，它们需要分多个阶段推出。通常会引入间接层，例如把文件的移动从使用处隐藏起来。这类间接会降低被移动文件的 page rank，让开发者更难发现新位置。此外，文件移动时查看次数通常会丢失，使情况更糟。由于这类代码库的全局重构相对罕见（大多数接口很少移动），最简单的解决方案是在这种过渡期手动提升文件。（或者等到迁移完成，让自然过程把文件在新位置的排名升上去。）

Query dependent signals · 与查询相关的信号

Query independent signals can be computed offline, so computational cost isn't a major concern, although it can be high. For example, for the page rank, the signal depends on the whole corpus and requires a MapReduce-like batch processing to calculate. Query dependent signals, which must be calculated for each query, should be cheap to compute. This means that they are restricted to the query and information quickly accessible from the index.

与查询无关的信号可以离线计算，因此计算成本不是主要顾虑，尽管它可能很高。例如，对 page rank，该信号依赖于整个语料库，需要类似 MapReduce 的批处理来计算。与查询相关的信号必须为每次查询计算，因此应当计算廉价。这意味着它们被限制在查询本身以及可从索引快速获取的信息之内。

Unlike web search, we don't just match on tokens. However, if there are clean token matches (that is, the search term matches with content with some form of breaks, such as whitespace, around it), a further boost is applied and case sensitivity is considered. This means, for example, a search for Point will score higher against Point *p than against appointed to the council.

与 Web 搜索不同，我们不只是在记号上匹配。然而，如果存在干净的记号匹配（即搜索词与周围带有某种分隔（如空白）的内容匹配），会施加进一步提升，并考虑大小写。这意味着，例如搜索 Point 时，对 “Point *p” 的打分高于对 “appointed to the council”。

For convenience, a default search matches filename and qualified symbols in addition to the actual file content. A user can specify the particular kind of match, but they don't need to. The scoring boosts symbol and filename matches over normal

为方便起见，默认搜索除了实际文件内容外，还会匹配文件名和限定符号。用户可以指定特定种类的匹配，但并非必须。打分对符号和文件名匹配给予高于普通

原书第 392 页

content matches to reflect the inferred intent of the developer. Just as with web searches, developers can add more terms to the search to make queries more specific. It's very common for a query to be qualified with hints about the filename (e.g., base or myproject). Scoring leverages this by boosting results where much of the query occurs in the full path of the potential result, putting such results ahead of those that contain only the words in random places in their content.

内容匹配的提升，以反映推断出的开发者意图。与 Web 搜索一样，开发者可以给搜索增加更多词，让查询更具体。查询被加上关于文件名的提示（例如 base 或 myproject）来“限定”是很常见的。打分利用这一点：把“查询的大部分出现在潜在结果完整路径中”的结果提升，让这类结果排在那些只在内容中随机位置包含这些词的结果之前。

Retrieval · 检索

Before a document can be scored, candidates that are likely to match the search query are found. This phase is called retrieval. Because it is not practical to retrieve all documents, but only retrieved documents can be scored, retrieval and scoring must work well together to find the most relevant documents. A typical example is to search for a class name. Depending on the popularity of the class, it can have thousands of usages, but potentially only one definition. If the search was not explicitly restricted to class definitions, retrieval of a fixed number of results might stop before the file with the single definition was reached. Obviously, the problem becomes more challenging as the codebase grows.

在一个文档能被打分之前，要先找到可能匹配搜索查询的候选。这一阶段称为检索。因为检索所有文档不现实，而只有被检索到的文档才能被打分，所以检索与打分必须良好配合，以找到最相关的文档。一个典型例子是搜索一个类名。根据该类的流行程度，它可能有数千处用法，但可能只有一个定义。如果搜索没有被显式限制为类定义，对固定数量结果的检索可能在到达那个含唯一定义的文件之前就停止了。显然，随着代码库增长，这个问题变得更具挑战。

The main challenge for the retrieval phase is to find the few highly relevant files among the bulk of less interesting ones. One solution that works quite well is called supplemental retrieval. The idea is to rewrite the original query into more specialized ones. In our example, this would mean that a supplemental query would restrict the search to only definitions and filenames and add the newly retrieved documents to the output of the retrieval phase. In a naive implementation of supplemental retrieval, more documents need to be scored, but the additional partial scoring information gained can be used to fully evaluate only the most promising documents from the retrieval phase.

检索阶段的主要挑战，是在大量不那么有趣的文件中找到那少数高度相关的文件。一种效果很好的方案叫做补充检索（supplemental retrieval）。其想法是把原始查询重写为更专门的查询。在我们的例子中，这意味着一个补充查询会把搜索限制为只查定义和文件名，并把新检索到的文档加入检索阶段的输出。在补充检索的朴素实现中，需要打分更多文档，但获得的额外部分打分信息，可用于只完整评估检索阶段中最有希望的文档。

Result diversity · 结果多样性

Another aspect of search is diversity of results, meaning trying to give the best results in multiple categories. A simple example would be to provide both the Java and Python matches for a simple function name, rather than filling the first page of results with one or the other.

搜索的另一个方面是结果的多样性，即尝试在多个类别中给出最好的结果。一个简单例子是：对一个简单函数名，同时给出 Java 和 Python 的匹配，而不是把第一页结果全被其中一种填满。

This is especially important when the intent of the user is not clear. One of the challenges with diversity is that there are many different categories—like functions, classes, filenames, local results, usages, tests, examples, and so on—into which results can be grouped, but that there isn't a lot of space in the UI to show results for all of them or even all combinations, nor would it always be desirable. Google's Code Search doesn't do this as well as web search does, but the drop-down list of suggested results (like the autocompletions of web search) is tweaked to provide a diverse set of top filenames, definitions, and matches in the user's current workspace.

当用户意图不明确时，这一点尤其重要。多样性的挑战之一是：结果可以被归入许多不同类别——如函数、类、文件名、本地结果、用法、测试、示例等等——但 UI 中没有太多空间为所有这些类别、乃至所有组合展示结果，而且也不总是可取的。Google 的 Code Search 在这方面做得不如 Web 搜索好，但建议结果的下拉列表（类似 Web 搜索的自动补全）经过了调整，以在用户当前工作区中提供一组多样化的顶级文件名、定义和匹配。

原书第 393 页

Selected Trade-Offs · 若干权衡

Implementing Code Search within a codebase the size of Google's—and keeping it responsive—involved making a variety of trade-offs. These are noted in the following section.

在 Google 规模的代码库中实现 Code Search——并保持它响应灵敏——涉及做出各种权衡。下面一节对此加以说明。

Completeness: Repository at Head · 完整性：处于 head 的仓库

We've seen that a larger codebase has negative consequences for search; for example, slower and more expensive indexing, slower queries, and noisier results. Can these costs be reduced by sacrificing completeness; in other words, leaving some content out of the index? The answer is yes, but with caution. Nontext files (binaries, images, videos, sound, etc.) are usually not meant to be read by humans and are dropped apart from their filename. Because they are huge, this saves a lot of resources. A more borderline case involves generated JavaScript files. Due to obfuscation and the loss of structure, they are pretty much unreadable for humans, so excluding them from the index is usually a good trade-off, reducing indexing resources and noise at the cost of completeness. Empirically, multimegabyte files rarely contain information relevant for developers, so excluding extreme cases is probably the correct choice.

我们已经看到，更大的代码库对搜索有负面后果；例如更慢、更贵的索引，更慢的查询，以及更嘈杂的结果。能否通过牺牲完整性来降低这些成本？换言之，把某些内容留在索引之外？答案是可以，但要谨慎。非文本文件（二进制、图像、视频、声音等）通常不是给人读的，除了文件名之外会被丢弃。由于它们巨大，这节省了大量资源。一个更暧昧的情形是生成的 JavaScript 文件。由于混淆和结构丢失，它们对人几乎不可读，因此把它们排除在索引之外通常是个不错的权衡——以完整性为代价，减少索引资源和噪声。经验上，数 MB 以上的文件很少包含与开发者相关的信息，因此排除极端情形大概是正确选择。

However, dropping files from the index has one big drawback. For developers to rely on Code Search, they need to be able to trust it. Unfortunately, it is generally impossible to give feedback about incomplete search results for a specific search if the dropped files weren't indexed in the first place. The resulting confusion and productivity loss for developers is a high price to pay for the saved resources. Even if developers are fully aware of the limitations, if they still need to perform their search, they will do so in an ad hoc and error-prone way. Given these rare but potentially high costs, we choose to err on the side of indexing too much, with quite high limits that are mostly picked to prevent abuse and guarantee system stability rather than to save resources.

然而，把文件从索引中丢弃有一个大弊端。开发者要依赖 Code Search，就需要能够信任它。遗憾的是，如果被丢弃的文件一开始就没被索引，通常就不可能对某个具体搜索给出“结果不完整”的反馈。由此给开发者造成的困惑和生产力损失，是为节省资源所付出的高昂代价。即便开发者完全知道这些限制，如果他们仍然需要执行搜索，也会以临时、易错的方式去做。鉴于这些罕见但潜在高昂的成本，我们选择宁多索引，设置相当高的限制——这些限制主要是为了防止滥用、保证系统稳定，而不是为了节省资源。

In the other direction, generated files aren't in the codebase but would often be useful to index. Currently they are not, because indexing them would require integrating the tools and configuration to create them, which would be a massive source of complexity, confusion, and latency.

在另一个方向上，生成的文件不在代码库中，但对它们做索引往往会有用。目前并没有这么做，因为索引它们需要集成创建它们的工具和配置，那将是复杂性、困惑和延迟的巨大来源。

Completeness: All Versus Most-Relevant Results · 完整性：全部结果 vs. 最相关结果

Normal search sacrifices completeness for speed, essentially gambling that ranking will ensure that the top results will contain all of the desired results. And indeed, for Code Search, ranked search is the more common case in which the user is looking for one particular thing, such as a function definition, potentially among millions of matches. However, sometimes developers want all results; for example, finding all occurrences of a particular symbol for refactoring. Needing all results is common for

普通搜索为速度牺牲完整性，本质上是在赌：排名会确保顶部结果包含所有想要的结果。确实，对 Code Search 而言，排名搜索是更常见的情形——用户在找某个具体东西，例如一个函数定义，可能在数百万匹配之中。然而，有时开发者想要所有结果；例如，为重构找出某个特定符号的所有出现。需要全部结果在

原书第 394 页

analysis, tooling, or refactoring, such as a global search and replace. The need to deliver all results is a fundamental difference to web search in which many shortcuts can be taken, such as to only consider highly ranked items.

分析、工具或重构中很常见，例如全局搜索并替换。需要交付全部结果，是与 Web 搜索的一个根本差异——在 Web 搜索中可以走很多捷径，例如只考虑高排名条目。

Being able to deliver all results for very large result sets has high cost, but we felt it was required for tooling, and for developers to trust the results. However, because for most queries only a few results are relevant (either there are only a few matches or only a few are interesting), we didn't want to sacrifice average speed for potential completeness.

能够为非常大的结果集交付全部结果，成本很高，但我们觉得这对工具、以及让开发者信任结果是必需的。然而，由于对大多数查询而言只有少数结果相关（要么只有少数匹配，要么只有少数有趣），我们不想为潜在的完整性牺牲平均速度。

To achieve both goals with one architecture, we split the codebase into shards with files ordered by their priority. Then, we usually need to consider only the matches to high priority files from each chunk. This is similar to how web search works. However, if requested, Code Search can fetch all results from each chunk, to guarantee finding all results. This lets us address both use cases, without typical searches being slowed down by the less frequently used capability of returning large, complete results sets. Results can also then be delivered in alphabetical order, rather than ranked, which is useful for some tools.

为了用一个架构同时达成两个目标，我们把代码库按文件优先级排序后切分成若干分片。然后，我们通常只需考虑每个分块中对高优先级文件的匹配。这与 Web 搜索的工作方式类似。然而，如果被要求，Code Search 可以从每个分块中取所有结果，以保证找到全部结果。这让我们能同时应对两种用例，而不会让典型搜索被“返回大型完整结果集”这一较少使用的能力拖慢。结果也可以按字母顺序而非排名交付，这对某些工具有用。

So, here the trade-off was a more complex implementation and API versus greater capabilities, rather than the more obvious latency versus completeness.

因此，这里的权衡是“更复杂的实现与 API”对“更强大的能力”，而不是更显而易见的“延迟对完整性”。

Completeness: Head Versus Branches Versus All History Versus Workspaces · 完整性：head、分支、全部历史、工作区

Related to the dimension of corpus size is the question of which code versions should be indexed: specifically, whether anything more than the current snapshot of code (head) should be indexed. System complexity, resource consumption, and overall cost increase drastically if more than a single file revision is indexed. To our knowledge, no IDE indexes anything but the current version of code. When looking at distributed version control systems like Git or Mercurial, a lot of their efficiency comes from the compression of their historical data. But the compactness of these representations becomes lost when constructing reverse indices. Another issue is that it is difficult to efficiently index graph structures, which are the basis for Distributed Version Control Systems.

与语料库大小这个维度相关的，是“应当索引哪些代码版本”的问题；具体说，除了代码的当前快照（head）之外，是否还应索引别的东西。如果索引多于单个文件修订，系统复杂性、资源消耗和总体成本都会急剧上升。据我们所知，没有任何 IDE 索引除当前版本代码之外的东西。当看 Git 或 Mercurial 这类分布式版本控制系统时，它们的效率很多来自对历史数据的压缩。但这些表示的紧凑性在构建倒排索引时就丧失了。另一个问题是：难以高效索引图结构，而图结构正是分布式版本控制系统的基础。

Although it is difficult to index multiple versions of a repository, doing so allows the exploration of how code has changed and finding deleted code. Within Google, Code Search indexes the (linear) Piper history. This means that the codebase can be

尽管索引一个仓库的多个版本很困难，但这样做能探索代码是如何变化的、并找到已删除的代码。在 Google 内部，Code Search 索引（线性的）Piper 历史。这意味着代码库可以

原书第 395 页

searched at an arbitrary snapshot of the code, for deleted code, or even for code authored by certain people.

在任意代码快照上被搜索、搜索已删除代码，甚至搜索由某些人编写的代码。

One big benefit is that obsolete code can now simply be deleted from the codebase. Before, code was often moved into directories marked as obsolete so that it could still be found later. The full history index also laid the foundation for searching effectively in people's workspaces (unsubmitted changes), which are synced to a specific snapshot of the codebase. For the future, a historical index opens up the possibility of interesting signals to use when ranking, such as authorship, code activity, and so on.

一个大好处是：过时代码现在可以直接从代码库中删除。以前，代码常被移到标记为“obsolete”的目录里，以便日后仍能找到。完整历史索引还为有效搜索人们的工作区（未提交变更）奠定了基础——这些工作区同步到代码库的某个特定快照。未来，历史索引开启了在排名时使用有趣信号的可能，例如作者身份、代码活跃度等等。

Workspaces are very different from the global repository:

工作区与全局仓库非常不同：

  • Each developer can have their own workspaces.

    每位开发者可以有自己的工作区。

  • There are usually a small number of changed files within a workspace.

    一个工作区内通常只有少量被修改的文件。

  • The files being worked on are changing frequently.

    正在处理的文件频繁变化。

  • A workspace exists only for a relatively short time period.

    一个工作区只存在相对较短的一段时间。

To provide value, a workspace index must reflect exactly the current state of the workspace.

为了提供价值，工作区索引必须精确反映工作区的当前状态。

Expressiveness: Token Versus Substring Versus Regex · 表达力：记号、子串 vs. 正则

The effect of scale is greatly influenced by the supported search feature set. Code Search supports regular expression (regex) search, which adds power to the query language, allowing whole groups of terms to be specified or excluded, and they can be used on any text, which is especially helpful for documents and languages for which deeper semantic tools don't exist.

规模的影响在很大程度上受所支持搜索功能集的影响。Code Search 支持正则表达式（regex）搜索，这为查询语言增加了能力，允许指定或排除整组词，而且它们可用于任何文本——这对那些没有更深入语义工具的文档和语言尤其有帮助。

Developers are also used to using regular expressions in other tools (e.g., grep) and contexts, so they provide powerful search without adding to a developer's cognitive load. This power comes at a cost given that creating an index to query them efficiently is challenging. What simpler options exist?

开发者也习惯于在其他工具（例如 grep）和上下文中使用正则表达式，因此它们在不增加开发者认知负荷的情况下提供强大搜索。这种能力是有代价的，因为创建一个能高效查询它们的索引颇具挑战。有哪些更简单的选项？

A token-based index (i.e., words) scales well because it stores only a fraction of the actual source code and is well supported by standard search engines. The downside is that many use cases are tricky or even impossible to realize efficiently with a token-based index when dealing with source code, which attaches meaning to many characters typically ignored when tokenizing. For example, searching for function() versus function(x), (x ^ y), or === myClass is difficult or impossible in most token-based searches.

基于记号（即单词）的索引可扩展性好，因为它只存储实际源代码的一小部分，且受标准搜索引擎良好支持。弊端是：处理源代码时，许多用例用基于记号的索引很难、甚至不可能高效实现——源代码赋予许多字符以意义，而这些字符在分词时通常被忽略。例如，在大多数基于记号的搜索中，搜索 function() 与 function(x)、(x ^ y)、或 === myClass 是困难或不可能的。

Another problem of tokenization is that tokenization of code identifiers is ill defined. Identifiers can be written in many ways, such as CamelCase, snake_case, or even justmashedtogether without any word separator. Finding an identifier when remembering only some of the words is a challenge for a token-based index.

分词的另一个问题是：代码标识符的分词没有良好定义。标识符可以用多种方式书写，例如 CamelCase、snake_case，甚至 justmashedtogether 没有任何单词分隔符。当只记得其中一部分词时找到一个标识符，对基于记号的索引是个挑战。

原书第 396 页

Tokenization also typically doesn't care about the case of letters (r versus R), and will often blur words; for example, reducing searching and searched to the same stem token search. This lack of precision is a significant problem when searching code. Finally, tokenization makes it impossible to search on whitespace or other word delimiters (commas, parentheses), which can be very important in code.

分词通常也不关心字母大小写（r 对 R），而且常常会把词模糊化；例如把 searching 和 searched 归约为同一个词干记号 search。这种精度的缺乏在搜索代码时是个重要问题。最后，分词使得不可能在空白或其他单词分隔符（逗号、括号）上搜索，而这些在代码中可能非常重要。

A next step up in searching power is full substring search in which any sequence of characters can be searched for. One fairly efficient way to provide this is via a trigram-based index. In its simplest form, the resulting index size is still much smaller than the original source code size. However, the small size comes at the cost of relatively low recall accuracy compared to other substring indices. This means slower queries because the nonmatches need to be filtered out of the result set. This is where a good compromise between index size, search latency, and resource consumption must be found that depends heavily on codebase size, resource availability, and searches per second.

搜索能力再上一个台阶是完整子串搜索，即可搜索任意字符序列。提供这种能力的一种相当高效的方式是通过基于三元组的索引。在其最简单形式下，所得索引大小仍远小于原始源代码大小。然而，这种小体积是以相对其他子串索引较低的召回精度为代价的。这意味着查询更慢，因为非匹配需要从结果集中过滤掉。正是在这里，必须在索引大小、搜索延迟和资源消耗之间找到一个良好折中，而这在很大程度上取决于代码库大小、资源可用性和每秒搜索数。

If a substring index is available, it's easy to extend it to allow regular expression searches. The basic idea is to convert the regular expression automaton into a set of substring searches. This conversion is straightforward for a trigram index and can be generalized to other substring indices. Because there is no perfect regular expression index, it will always be possible to construct queries that result in a brute-force search. However, given that only a small fraction of user queries are complex regular expressions, in practice, the approximation via substring indices works very well.

如果有子串索引，可以很容易地把它扩展到支持正则表达式搜索。基本想法是把正则表达式自动机转换为一组子串搜索。这种转换对三元组索引很直接，并可推广到其他子串索引。由于不存在完美的正则表达式索引，总可能构造出导致暴力搜索的查询。然而，由于只有一小部分用户查询是复杂正则表达式，实践中通过子串索引的近似效果非常好。

Conclusion · 小结

Code Search grew from an organic replacement for grep into a central tool boosting developer productivity, leveraging Google's web search technology along the way. What does this mean for you, though? If you are on a small project that easily fits in your IDE, probably not much. If you are responsible for the productivity of engineers on a larger codebase, there are probably some insights to be gained.

Code Search 从一个 grep 的自然替代品，成长为一个提升开发者生产力的核心工具，一路走来还利用了 Google 的 Web 搜索技术。但这对你意味着什么？如果你在一个能轻松装进 IDE 的小项目里，大概没什么。如果你负责较大代码库上工程师的生产力，或许能获得一些洞见。

The most important one is perhaps obvious: understanding code is key to developing and maintaining it, and this means that investing in understanding code will yield dividends that might be difficult to measure, but are real. Every feature we added to Code Search was and is used by developers to help them in their daily work (admittedly some more than others). Two of the most important features, Kythe integration (i.e., adding semantic code understanding) and finding working examples, are also the most clearly tied to understanding code (versus, for example, finding it, or seeing

最重要的一点也许很显然：理解代码是开发和维护它的关键，这意味着投资于理解代码会带来或许难以衡量、但真实存在的红利。我们加到 Code Search 上的每一个特性，过去和现在都被开发者用于帮助他们的日常工作（诚然有些用得更多）。其中两个最重要的特性——Kythe 集成（即增加语义化代码理解）和查找可工作的示例——也最明显地与“理解代码”相关（而不是例如“找到代码”或“看到

how it's changed). In terms of tool impact, no one uses a tool that they don't know exists, so it is also important to make developers aware of the available tooling—at Google, it is part of Noogler training, the onboarding training for newly hired software engineers.

它是如何变化的）。就工具影响力而言，没有人会使用一个自己不知道存在的工具，因此让开发者知道有哪些可用工具也很重要——在 Google，这是 Noogler 培训（新入职软件工程师的入职培训）的一部分。

For you, this might mean setting up a standard indexing profile for IDEs, sharing knowledge about egrep, running ctags, or setting up some custom indexing tooling, like Code Search. Whatever you do, it will almost certainly be used, and used more, and in different ways than you expected—and your developers will benefit.

对你而言，这可能意味着为 IDE 设置一个标准索引配置、分享关于 egrep 的知识、运行 ctags，或搭建一些自定义索引工具，比如 Code Search。无论你做什么，它几乎肯定会被使用、被更频繁地使用、并以你意料之外的方式被使用——而你的开发者将从中受益。

TL;DRs · 本章要点

  • Helping your developers understand code can be a big boost to engineering productivity. At Google, the key tool for this is Code Search.

    帮助你的开发者理解代码，可以极大提升工程生产力。在 Google，用于此的关键工具是 Code Search。

  • Code Search has additional value as a basis for other tools and as a central, standard place that all documentation and developer tools link to.

    Code Search 还有额外价值：它是其他工具的基础，也是所有文档和开发者工具链接到的中央、标准位置。

  • The huge size of the Google codebase made a custom tool—as opposed to, for example, grep or an IDE's indexing—necessary.

    Google 代码库的巨大规模，使得一个自定义工具——而非例如 grep 或 IDE 的索引——成为必要。

  • As an interactive tool, Code Search must be fast, allowing a question and answer workflow. It is expected to have low latency in every respect: search, browsing, and indexing.

    作为一个交互式工具，Code Search 必须快，以支持“问—答”工作流。它在各方面都被期望低延迟：搜索、浏览和索引。

  • It will be widely used only if it is trusted, and will be trusted only if it indexes all code, gives all results, and gives the desired results first. However, earlier, less powerful, versions were both useful and used, as long as their limits were understood.

    它只有在被信任时才会被广泛使用，而只有在它索引全部代码、给出全部结果、并把想要的结果排在最前时才会被信任。然而，更早、功能较弱的版本，只要其局限被理解，也同样有用、被使用。
